newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar hit by pre-EU tender hedging.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar hit by pre-EU tender hedging.

text.p: A bout of nervous selling and liquidation in early trading cut back some of the recent gains in London white sugar prices on Wednesday morning.
By 1030 GMT near August was trading at $327.50 a tonne, down $3.30 from Tuesday's close, having at one stage touched $327.00. Total turnover was 562 lots.
Market sources said that some trade houses had formulated their bids for subsidy at today's EU weekly white sugar tender on the basis of Tuesday's firm closing futures market levels.
But a lack of follow through to Tuesday's good fund buying interest meant pre-tender hedging orders this morning came to an uncreceptive market.
The consequent fall in prices touched off some nervous profittaking in a market which was due for a downward correction after recent strength, sources said.
Paris was also hit by similar business and the August position at 10.30 GMT was trading at $327.50, down $2.10 a tonne, and turnover was 379 lots.
